name: The Battery Atlanta
lesson: A stadium district built to capture visitor spending inside its own boundary, with large parking supply. Nearby businesses outside the district saw less spillover than promised.
source: General reference: verify with a primary study before the workshop

name: Navy Yard / Nationals Park
lesson: A stadium next to an existing Metro station. Transit carried much of the event crowd and helped make the land around it valuable.
source: General reference: verify before the workshop

name: DC Chinatown and Capital One Arena
lesson: After the arena opened, property values rose and most Chinese residents and businesses were displaced. Rules requiring Chinese-language signs kept the look but not the community. Chicago Chinatown leaders cite this case.
source: Press coverage of Chinatown concerns (2025–26); verify before the workshop

name: Atlantic Yards / Pacific Park
lesson: An arena-led megaproject with a CBA. Promised affordable housing and jobs arrived years late, and the CBA proved hard to enforce.
source: General reference: verify before the workshop

name: Hudson Yards
lesson: Large public financing, including tax diversions and infrastructure bonds, went into a private district. How much public money went in is still disputed.
source: General reference: verify before the workshop

name: Mission Bay
lesson: A former rail yard by the water redeveloped with a required share of open space and affordable housing.
source: General reference: verify before the workshop

name: Woodlawn Housing Preservation Ordinance
lesson: Faced with the Obama Center, residents won an ordinance through City Council rather than a CBA with a private party. It set affordable housing protections on city-owned land.
